text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Forty-six people have been killed and another 255 injured by whirlwinds and flash floods throughout Vietnam in the first seven months of this year.
-- An International Monetary Fund mission is in Vietnam to review the country's economic programmes.
-- Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee acting Chairman, Vo Viet Thanh has said barriers to the promotion of investment should be cleared.
-- The U.S.-based Overseas Private Investmnet Corporation is expected to get the go-ahead to start operations in Vietnam.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has been warmly welcomed in Vientiane by Laotian Prime Minister Khamtay Siphandone.
-- Water levels in the Mekong River are expected to reach the maximum warning stage in the next few days.
-- 128,000 hectares of paddy fields have been submerged by flooding in the northern Red River delta.
-- Hanoi city has defined the restructuring of state enterprises as its prime task.
-- More than 80 percent of the summer-autumn rice crop has been harvested in Mekong delta provinces.
-- Negotiations between Vietnam and the United States are continuing with a view to reaching an anti-narcotics agreement before October 1, a U.S. official has said.
